sections.what_happened: CEC count advanced from 6.5% of polls (320,750 valid votes, 02:39 Israel time) to a party-level table at 18.8% reporting (952,495 total votes, 950,946 valid) with the infobox reporting level at 20.1% as of 03:53 Israel time (05:53 ). At the 18.8% table: Likud 229,760 votes (24.16%, table seat figure 32), Yashar 152,993 (16.09%, 22), Together 83,575 (8.79%, 12), Yisrael Beiteinu 66,096 (6.95%, 9), UTJ 63,436 (6.67%, 9), Otzma Yehudit 60,773 (6.39%, 8), Joint List 55,816 (5.87%, 7), Shas 53,545 (5.63%, 7), Democrats 53,282 (5.60%, 6), RZP-Zehut 51,411 (5.41%, 7). Table-implied blocs (NOT an official allocation, NOT a projection): Netanyahu bloc 63, opposition bloc 49, Arab parties 7 (sums to 119 in the table). Ra'am sits at 26,217 votes (2.76%) -- BELOW the 3.25% threshold in this partial, with a table figure of 0 seats, versus 7 seats in the exit polls. Exit-poll baseline unchanged: opposition 52-53, Netanyahu bloc 50, Arab parties 17-18, neither near 61; turnout 77.7%. The early partial and the exit polls cannot both describe the final result; the partial covers only ~1/5 of the vote and early-reporting areas skew the picture (same warning as at 6.5%).
sections.what_verified: Count figures: 1 declared-tier family -- the CEC itself (T1 official/primary data) as displayed by the Wikipedia table; Wikipedia holds NO declared tier and adds no corroboration. Exit-poll baseline: Reuters T1 + Channels 12/13/Kan via Times of Israel T3 (prior scans). Gate: primary_source_single_family=true for the count figures.
sections.what_disputed: Early partials are unrepresentative by construction: ~80% of votes uncounted, double-envelope votes (soldiers, diplomats, prisoners, hospital patients) counted days later, and the counted set so far visibly under-represents Arab-party voters versus every exit poll (Ra'am 2.76% in partial vs 7 exit-poll seats; Joint List 5.87% vs 11-12). Channel 14's pro-Netanyahu 60-seat projection is an outlier against the three major networks and is not a count. The table's own seat column is if-counted-votes-were-final arithmetic, not seats won.
sections.why_matters: THE COUNT FLIPS THE STORY: 20% counted, Likud leads, Arab kingmakers nearly vanish -- but 80% of ballots are still out. Hard number in title + exit-poll-vs-ballot reveal frame; never present the partial as a result.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE to totw-20261028-0000-09/0100-01/0200-01/0300-01/0400-01/0500-01 (Israel election night) -- CEC real count jumps from 6.5% to ~20% reporting; early partial STILL favours Netanyahu bloc and nearly erases Arab parties, opposite to exit polls, but ~80% uncounted

totw_analysis: Our read: THE COUNT FLIPS THE STORY: 20% counted, Likud leads, Arab kingmakers nearly vanish -- but 80% of ballots are still out. Hard number in title + exit-poll-vs-ballot reveal frame; never present the partial as a result. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Exit polls vs real ballots: did the polls miss a Netanyahu-bloc surge, or does the early count just reflect which areas reported first -- and will the Arab parties, crowned kingmakers by the exit polls, survive the threshold in the real count?
